title: Chat parser and ledger calculation choices
decision: Helper agents chose, and the orchestrator accepted: entries under open dispute still receive payments in the oldest-first allocation and still count in the balance and in the payment history indicator, and are left out only of the amounts a reminder may mention (BR-13); the indicator counts only debt whose promised date has passed, measured against the current promised date (BR-9); an entry promised for today is due today, not overdue; end of week means the coming Sunday; the percentage rounds halves up; the chat parser reads space and dot as thousands separators and a comma always as a decimal mark, accepts the thousand words k, ming and their Russian forms, and answers that a message is ambiguous instead of guessing. The full lists are in the two pull requests
context: Decided by an agent during the autonomous build under DEC-020; implemented and awaiting the founder's review
chosen_option: Choices as listed in pull requests 11 and 12
rationale: The approved rules BR-9 and BR-13 leave these points open. Each choice is the one that never understates what a customer owes and never claims lateness on the promised day
